title: Regional pinning and staleness SLA for analytics streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and internal compliance require firm controls so tenant usage events and derivative analytics either never leave a specified legal region or are allowed to be replicated only under constrained staleness/retention policies. Current pipeline mirrors usage streams globally with no tenant-level pinning and no staleness SLAs, which prevents sales/legal from approving Private/VPC rollouts for regulated customers.

Objective: Implement a control-plane driven regional pinning feature for analytics streams plus an operationally enforceable staleness SLA for any cross-region replication. The feature must: 1) let Console and APIs declare per-tenant residency preferences (strict, soft, or multi); 2) provide a migration path for existing tenants; 3) expose metrics and alerts for replication lag and policy violations; 4) interoperate with Dedicated/Private placements and KMS boundaries.

Proposed design (high level):
- Residency controller: a Console-backend service (residency-controller) that stores tenant residency policy and orchestrates placement decisions for analytics ingestion and replication workers.
- Placement modes:
  - strict_pin: write and primary read must remain in tenant_region; no streaming replication to other regions except cold-archive snapshots (encrypted and controlled).
  - soft_pin: primary write in tenant_region; asynchronous replication allowed to regional read replicas with a configured staleness SLA (e.g., 60s default, configurable up to 5m).
  - multi: no residency constraints (current default).
- Replication topology: primary-local streaming (Kafka-like segments) with cross-region consumer pipelines that apply ordering guarantees per-tenant. Cross-region replicas are eventually consistent and tagged with replication_timestamp for staleness validation.
- Staleness SLA enforcement: consumers/route controllers will evaluate replication_timestamp; if replica_lag > SLA, the control plane will: a) mark replica as stale in dashboards, b) route reads to primary where possible, c) trigger alerting and optional rollback of any canary read routing.
- Audit and compliance: every residency change is recorded with actor, timestamp, justification, and linked to audit logs and optional legal_tag. Residency changes require two-step approval for tenants with customer_impact=high.
- Console/API: admin endpoints to set residency with fields {region_preference, mode, staleness_seconds, legal_tag}. Console UX will show current replication lag and region map.

Migration strategy:
- Phase 1 (opt-in): New tenants default to soft_pin with a conservative SLA (120s) for EU pilot customers.
- Phase 2 (data backfill): For existing tenants opting into strict_pin, a background migration job copies historical analytic blobs into a region-local store and switches the event routing to region-local primary. During migration, dual-write will be enabled for a short window to avoid data loss.
- Phase 3 (enforcement): After pilot verification, enable policy checks on write paths that prevent accidental cross-region forwarding for strict_pin tenants.

Monitoring + SLOs:
- Key metrics: replication_lag_seconds{tenant,region}, replication_error_count{tenant}, last_replicated_offset{tenant,region}, policy_violation_count, percent_reads_served_locally.
- Alerts: replication_lag_seconds > configured_sla for >2 minutes, policy_violation_count > 0.
- Dashboards: per-tenant residency summary, regional capacity consumed by pinned tenants, cross-region egress costs per tenant.

Security & KMS note: Cross-region replication of encrypted payloads must honor KMS key policies. For strict_pin tenants, keys must be region-local; cross-region replication is only allowed if keys permit decryption in destination (rare). Work with Security to document allowed patterns.

Rollout plan (canary):
1) Feature-flag residency-controller and API endpoints (backend-only) for internal test tenants.
2) Enable Console UI and onboarding flows for beta customers (EU pilot).
3) Monitor metrics for 2 weeks, iterate on lag tuning and autoscaling for replication workers.
4) Gradual expansion to broader tenant set once staleness SLA and costs are acceptable.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Strong ordering vs performance: enforcing strict tenant-affinity and ordering per-tenant increases coordination cost. We will favor per-tenant partitioning (single writer) to minimize cross-tenant coupling.
- Cold archive strategy: whether to allow encrypted cold copies in other regions for disaster recovery while still claiming "data residency" (we propose storing immutable snapshots but keep strict access controls and legal_tag metadata).
- Cost model: pinned-tenants increase regional storage and egress. Need finance to propose pricing or Dedicated commitments.

Acceptance criteria:
- Residency API endpoints implemented and documented in Console backend.
- Residency controller persists per-tenant policy and exposes a sync endpoint for ingestion workers.
- Replication pipeline enforces staleness SLA checks and emits metrics described above.
- Migration jobs for historical data exist as idempotent batch jobs and succeed for a test tenant.
- End-to-end integration test and canary deployed to internal EU pilot with alerts and dashboards.

Notes on compatibility: This design must remain compatible with Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private deployments; the residency-controller should be able to operate in both hosted control-plane and customer-managed control-plane modes (configuration flag).
acceptance_criteria: residency-controller persists policy and serves placement decisions over gRPC/HTTP
replication workers emit replication_lag_seconds and honor SLA for soft_pin tenants
migration job completed for a test tenant with zero data loss
Console shows per-tenant residency status and replication lag
